questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have visited the city several times before and really liked it. Therefore, I thought it would be interesting to attend a semester there. I had also heard great things about the university from others who had been there on exchange.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Overall, I think it was quite easy to find the information that I needed to know upon arrival as there were several information meetings, guided tours, etc. The visiting students office was also very helpful with all my questions.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: When I arrived at my study destination, there were information meetings for visiting students where they informed us of all the practical aspects of the exchange and where we could meet other exchange students. There was also a lunch for all visiting students at my faculty where we could meet each other and ask questions about our exchange.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found it quite easy to find off campus housing as I applied through the accommodation hub and was offered a room within a few days after the deadline. I was not able to apply before close to the deadline, but if possible, I would recommend applying for accommodation through the university as soon as possible.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You may end up spending quite some time and money on public transport. You can either buy a travel card that grants you unlimited public transport within the city or rent a bike.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I contacted the visiting students office by mail a month before the semester began as I had not heard anything about course registration. They informed me that I should contact the School, which I did. They then asked me to fill out a document with five priorities for courses and granted me my top three priorities.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any information about course registration, but both the visiting students office and the School were very helpful when I contacted them.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful. I got my three top priorities.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you do not hear anything from them about course registration, contact them. They are very helpful.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level of courses is comparable with the level of courses as UCPH. It was mostly academic articles like at UCPH. The amount of reading was the same, maybe a bit less.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
I had three different kinds of classes: lectures, seminars and tutorials. Lectures are the same as at UCPH and the seminars are comparable to classes (holdtimer) at UCPH. In tutorials, you sit in a small class of around 10 people and discuss the readings and the questions of the week. The questions are provided in advance so you can prepare for the discussions in the tutorial. I found this very rewarding as it enabled you to really discuss the readings in depth.

Seminars are 2x50 minutes whereas lectures and tutorials are 50 minutes each.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1) Politics and Governance of Crisis
2) Russia in Global Politics
3) International Security

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all three courses, but especially Russia in Global Politics. It was such a fascinating course with interesting readings and the teacher was really good at disseminating knowledge and structuring the course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I did not really encounter any unexpected costs. I thought I might have to buy books, but there were no books on any of my courses' reading lists.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The accommodation and costs for my phone were more expensive than I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were many different activities available at the host institution. At the beginning of the semester, there is a kind of activities fair where you are introduced to all the societies at the university that you can join.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to engage in as many as possible as this is probably the best way to meet new people. I really enjoyed the yoga society as it was a nice break from the studies and the yoga instructors were very good. The yoga society also held social events.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend other visiting students to explore the city and travel to other cities such as Stirling, Glasgow and North Berwick which are all close to Edinburgh and easy to visit by train.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it quite easy to adjust to the local culture. Everyone was very kind and welcoming.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not really find any cultural differences challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How welcoming and kind all people were to me – and very polite on public transport.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) If you struggle with anything, academic or non-academic, please reach out to them. They are very kind and helpful.
2) Do not worry about writing essays. There are workshops and the teachers are very understanding and can help you with all your questions.
3) Do not stress about all the practical aspects. It may seem daunting at first, but there are so many people you can reach out to for help.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a Facebook group for KU students in the UK. In there, you can reach out to hear if others are going to the same university as you. I found it really helpful to know others who were in the same position as me, who I could share the experience with and talk with about practical aspects.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I really improved my English and, I think, became more confident both academically and non-academically.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge during my exchange was that it was quite difficult to meet people. There was not really any community in my accommodation and it could therefore be quite lonely at times.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
